target: Estuve en una conferencia toda la semana.
english: I was at a conference all week.
tip: Toda la semana sounds ongoing, but it's a closed box – the week ended. Bounded durations take preterite: estuve, not estaba, no matter how long it dragged on.

target: Siempre como en la oficina los martes.
english: I always eat at the office on Tuesdays.
tip: No 'on' before days – the article does that job: 'los martes' = the Tuesdays = on Tuesdays (every one). El martes alone = this coming Tuesday.

target: Mientras hablaba por teléfono, llegó el jefe.
english: While I was talking on the phone, the boss arrived.
tip: Imperfecto (hablaba) for ongoing action + pretérito (llegó) for interruption.

target: Me pusieron una multa por estacionar en doble fila.
english: I got a fine for parking in a no-parking zone.
tip: Who fined you? Just 'they': 'me pusieron una multa' = they put a fine on me. Spanish uses an anonymous 3rd-plural where English goes passive (I got fined).

target: Trabajo por las mañanas y estudio por las tardes.
english: I work in the mornings and study in the afternoons.
tip: Por + time period = during: por la mañana, por la tarde, por la noche.

target: Me di una ducha rápida porque no tenía mucho tiempo.
english: I took a quick shower because I didn't have much time.
tip: Two pasts, two lenses: me di una ducha is the single done event (preterite), no tenía mucho tiempo is the background condition it happened against (imperfect).

target: Habríamos adoptado un perro si el departamento fuera más grande.
english: We would have adopted a dog if the apartment were bigger.
tip: 'Departamento' looks like 'department', but in Latin America it's an apartment. Spain says piso for a flat; context decides office division vs home.

target: Se me fue el santo al cielo y olvidé la cita.
english: My mind went blank and I forgot the appointment.
tip: Note it's se me fue, not fui: the 'accidental se' frames forgetting as something that happened TO you – the saint left on his own, and me marks you as the innocent victim.

target: Mientras hablaba por teléfono, el gato se subió a la mesa.
english: While talking on the phone, the cat jumped on the table.
tip: Imperfect (hablaba) for background action + preterite (se subió) for the sudden event.

target: No quise decir eso; me expresé mal.
english: I didn't mean that – i expressed myself poorly.
tip: 'Querer decir' = literally 'to want to say' = to mean. 'No quise decir eso' = I didn't mean that – Spanish treats meaning as what you wanted your words to say.

target: El paisaje era tan bonito que paramos para hacer fotos.
english: The landscape was so beautiful that we stopped to take photos.
tip: "Tan...que" = so...that: "Es tan alto que no cabe." Intensifier + adjective/adverb + que + result clause.

target: Se lo dije ayer.
english: I told him yesterday.
tip: Double object pronouns: indirect (le/les) + direct (lo/la) → "se lo." Le becomes se before lo/la to avoid "le lo." "Se lo dije" = I told it to him.

target: Se me olvidó comprar pan.
english: I forgot to buy bread.
tip: "Se me olvidó" – accidental/unintentional construction with "se".

target: No creía que fuera posible.
english: I didn't believe it was possible.
tip: Deny a belief and the verb goes subjunctive: "No creía que fuera posible" – fuera, not era. Creía que era = believed it was; no creía flips the mood.

target: Ella llevaba un vestido rojo.
english: She was wearing a red dress.
tip: Here 'llevaba' is imperfect – the scene-setting past for describing people, places, weather, and time.

target: Te lo dije ayer, ¿no te acuerdas?
english: I told you yesterday, don't you remember?
tip: Double object pronouns: te (indirect) + lo (direct) before conjugated verb.

target: Antes había más árboles en esta calle.
english: There used to be more trees on this street.
tip: "There WERE more trees," yet Spanish says "había," never habían. Había is frozen singular no matter how many árboles – it marks existence, not a plural subject.

target: El día en que nos conocimos llovía mucho.
english: The day we met it was raining a lot.
tip: "Nos conocimos" isn't "we knew each other" – conocer in preterite means MET. Tense flips the meaning: conocía = knew, conocimos = met for the first time.

target: Me pongo el abrigo porque hace frío fuera.
english: I put on my coat because it's cold outside.
tip: Ponerse is literally 'to put onto oneself' – and because me pongo already says whose body the coat lands on, Spanish uses el abrigo, not 'my' coat.

target: Si me hubieras escuchado, no tendríamos este problema.
english: If you had listened to me, we wouldn't have this problem.
tip: 'Hubieras escuchado' (past condition) pairs with 'tendríamos' (present result). Spanish mixes the two when a past mistake still affects the present.

target: El vuelo iba lleno y no pudimos sentarnos juntos.
english: The flight was full and we couldn't sit together.
tip: Poder in the preterite is loaded: no pudimos means we actually tried to sit together and failed. Imperfect no podíamos would just describe a general inability.

target: ¿Estás listo para salir o todavía no estás preparado?
english: Are you ready to leave or aren't you ready yet?
tip: "¿Estás listo?" asks if you're ready – but eres listo would call you clever! Listo changes meaning with ser/estar; estar = the ready-to-go state.

target: La reunión es a las tres en la sala grande.
english: The meeting is at three in the big room.
tip: Ser for events: "La reunión es a las tres." Events use ser for when/where they take place.

target: Me probé unos pantalones grises pero me quedaban demasiado grandes.
english: I tried on some gray pants but they were too big for me.
tip: Clothes fit backwards in Spanish: "me quedaban demasiado grandes" – the pants stayed-too-big ON me. Quedar works like gustar: the garment acts, you receive.

target: Me quedé dormido en el autobús.
english: I fell asleep on the bus.
tip: "Me quedé dormido" looks like "I stayed asleep" but means I FELL asleep – quedarse marks slipping into a new state. That's how you nod off on the bus.

target: Mientras ella cocinaba, yo ponía la mesa.
english: While she cooked, I set the table.
tip: Imperfect for simultaneous past actions: "Mientras yo cocinaba, él leía." Two ongoing actions happening at the same time → both in imperfect.

target: Cuando era niño, vivía en el campo.
english: When I was a kid, I lived in the countryside.
tip: Here 'vivía' is imperfect: use it for habitual past – repeated actions, routines, and 'used to'.

target: Perdona, ¿sabes dónde está la parada más cercana?
english: Excuse me, do you know where the nearest stop is?
tip: "Perdona" is the informal attention-getter (tú). Fine for strangers your age; switch to perdone for elders or formal settings – same word, usted ending.

target: A pesar de ser lunes, la oficina estaba vacía.
english: Despite it being Monday, the office was empty.
tip: A pesar de + infinitive – despite + -ing.

target: Mi suegra nos invita a comer todos los domingos.
english: My mother-in-law invites us over for lunch every Sunday.
tip: Why "comer" for one specific meal? In Spain comer IS the midday meal – the day's main event, around 2pm. "Nos invita a comer" = big Sunday lunch, not a bite.
